label: heart-s7
summary: The model scores heart-disease risk as a linear score of direct input edges plus three gates, added on the logit scale. The direct score carries most of the ranking (training AUC 0.947, falling to 0.811 without it), and its largest term is the number of major vessels coloured by fluoroscopy (2.61 per sd); female sex lowers it directly (-1.57 per sd on the female indicator). An ST-depression gate, open for 116 training patients, adds risk once ST depression passes a threshold that a reversible thallium defect lowers and a downsloping segment raises. A second gate gives back part of the female discount to women with exercise-induced angina: it acts on 19 of the 19 such women and on 0 of the 63 men with exercise angina, so it is fitted to a small group. A third gate lowers risk for a high maximum heart rate, opening at a lower rate with non-anginal chest pain; it is open for 74 patients and is the least important part (AUC 0.945 without it).
